chunks: A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Shammun from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman from Misma' from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When one of you looks at a beautiful woman, let him go to his wife, for what is with her is like what is with her.' A man stood up and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, if he does not have a wife, what should he do?' He said: 'Let him raise his gaze to the sky, let him fear Him, and let him ask Him from His generosity.'
ai.seo_question: What should a Muslim do if he sees a beautiful woman but is not married?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi outlines a practical spiritual remedy for the fitnah of visual attraction, prioritizing the sanctity of one's own spouse as a sufficient counterpart to external beauty. For the unmarried, it prescribes a shift in focus from the material to the divine by gazing at the sky, thereby cultivating taqwa (God-consciousness) and reliance on Allah's bounty. This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on internalizing faith through sensory redirection and continuous divine surveillance.
